cells.tense: You are weighing something fairly right now, with the pen still in your hand.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Pick one arrangement that was right when you set it and isn't anymore. Let it end, and see how the level holds without you holding it.
cells.core:
Someone brings you a mess of feeling, and you can feel the whole of it and still call it evenly. Nobody gets punished for having a feeling, and no one's feeling tips the scale. You let it finish before you rule, and the ruling lands after, not over. Seen whole, it stays level.

What that takes is time you don't always want to spend: some arrangements stay standing past the years they served, because they were right once and you go on honouring them. Letting one of those end costs only the habit. The level holds without you holding it, and no one needs to be told why.
cells.sheetLine: You feel it all and still call it fairly.

cells.tense: You will have ruled on the hurt before it has finished happening.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: The next hurt that reaches you, carry it a day with no verdict — as a load, not a case, the way a builder carries stone before deciding what wall it's for.
cells.core:
A hurt comes to you and the ruling on whether it was proportionate is already in, before it has had its hour. Fairness that fast starts to feel, to the people under it, like a court they did not know they walked into. The whole pattern arrives early, and it rules early too.

What this part of you asks for instead is weight carried rather than settled. The hurt that reaches you next, carry it a day with no verdict — as a load, not a case, the way a builder carries stone before deciding what wall it is for. The ruling will be shorter for the wait, and the person it concerns will be able to hear it.
cells.sheetLine: You're ruling on feelings while they're still being felt.

cells.tense: You saw what was unfair and you stopped calling it, some time back.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Take one unfair situation and set down your questions about it, then answer them on the page in order. Read it back and see what the answers say.
cells.core:
When you can call an unfair thing cleanly, the room settles, and people stop carrying what should be shared. You have done that. What has gone quiet is the calling itself — something is out of proportion, and the one who could say so has stepped back from saying it. The quiet has a cost, and it comes out of the people near it.

Method does here what nerve will not. Set down your questions about one unfair situation, then answer them on the page in order, and read it back. That needs nothing from you but the page. The call arrives half made, in your own handwriting, and this part of you has something to recognise again.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's unfair and you've stopped calling it.

cells.tense: You are keeping things level between the people near you, and telling it as if you stay out of it.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Hear the next argument near you all the way through as someone learning it, not someone who already has the ruling — before you do the thing you do to even it out.
cells.core:
Things between the people close to you stay in proportion because you quietly keep them there — a word here, a weight shifted there. To hear you tell it, you stay out of it. There is a keeper, and the keeper's story is that of a bystander. The people being kept level have not believed that once, and they do not need to.

What returns it to you is smaller than the work: listen first, as a student of the argument rather than its judge. Hear the next argument near you all the way through before you do the thing you do to even it out. You will hear the part you usually smooth over, and the work gets seen from the inside, by the one doing it. Nothing changes but that.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the level between people while saying you stay out of it.
